name: Reuben
description: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and Israel heard it. That is fornication such as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father's wife.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

points: Reuben delivered him out of their hands: cast him into this pit, but lay no hand upon him; he meant to return him to his father.

note.label: Genesis 37: Joseph the Dreamer

points: Reuben returned unto the pit, and Joseph was not in the pit, and he rent his clothes. Reuben suggested the pit because his plan was to go back and save Joseph. Remember the characteristic of Reuben; it's going to play a part later on.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

points: Reuben answered them, spake I not unto you, saying, do not sin against the child? Reuben was the one who would not have Joseph slain, but said to sell him not and lay no hand on him.

note.label: Genesis 42: Joseph's Brethren Bow Down in Egypt

points: Reuben spake unto his father, saying, slay my two sons, if I bring him not to thee. There's the characteristic of Reuben again, from when they first put Joseph in the pit.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

points: Thy two sons Ephraim and Manasseh, as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine. Jacob took Joseph's sons as his own, so the blessings that came upon Jacob's sons came upon Ephraim and Manasseh also; they became children of Israel, partakers of the same promises as the rest of the sons of Jacob.

note.label: Genesis 48: Ephraim and Manasseh Blessed as Sons of Israel

points: Reuben is the so-called Seminole Indian today. Reuben, thou art my firstborn, the beginning of my strength: the firstborn is the father's posterity, and the excellency of dignity and the excellency of power belonged to him; the Seminoles were great warriors.

note.label: Genesis 49: What Shall Befall the Twelve Tribes in the Last Days

points: Don't think the northern kingdom is weak — Reuben and Ephraim had their own armies. Our formations are not yet what they will be.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: On the south side was the standard of the camp of Reuben, with Elizur the son of Shedeur as captain, and by him Simeon under Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai and Gad under Eliasaph the son of Reuel.

note.label: Numbers 2: The Order of the Camps About the Tabernacle

points: Judah's camp was 186,400 throughout their armies. Reuben's was 151,450, Ephraim's 108,100, each set in its rank, first, second and third. Armies inside the army.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: All that were numbered in the camp of Reuben were an hundred thousand and fifty and one thousand and four hundred and fifty, which is 151,450 throughout their armies; and they set forth in the second rank.

note.label: Numbers 2: The Order of the Camps About the Tabernacle

points: The children of Reuben and Gad had a very great multitude of cattle, and when they saw that Jazer and Gilead was a place for cattle, they asked Moses for that land and said, bring us not over Jordan.

note.label: Numbers 32: The Inheritance of Reuben and Gad on This Side Jordan

points: Moses gave unto the children of Gad and of Reuben and unto half the tribe of Manasseh the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, the land with the cities thereof, and they built their cities and folds for sheep.

note.label: Numbers 32: The Inheritance of Reuben and Gad on This Side Jordan

points: What he did unto Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, the son of Reuben: the earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up, their households, their tents, and all the substance in their possession, in the midst of all Israel.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

points: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali were to stand upon mount Ebal to curse. Half the tribes stood on one side and half on the other, one saying one thing and the other answering.

note.label: Deuteronomy 27: Write the Law upon Stones

points: Let Reuben live, and not die; and let not his men be few. Reuben is the Seminole Indians: under Andrew Jackson the Indian removal campaign set out to exterminate them, and many were slaughtered, but they were not able to kill them all.
They tried it, but they were not fully successful; that is why the blessing says let Reuben live, and not die.

note.label: Deuteronomy 33: The Blessing of Moses, Identifying the Tribes in the Last Days

points: The children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh passed over armed before the children of Israel, about forty thousand prepared for war, keeping the word they gave Moses: suited for battle with their brethren before returning to enjoy their own land on the other side.

note.label: Joshua 4: The Twelve Stone Memorial

points: Them did Moses the servant of the LORD and the children of Israel smite, and Moses gave their land for a possession unto the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh. Look up a map of the Jordan river and the twelve tribes and you will see the split of where Reuben, Gad, and half Manasseh dwelt, on the east side of Jordan.

note.label: Joshua 12: The Thirty and One Kings

points: Moses gave the tribe of the children of Reuben their inheritance according to their families: from Aroer on the bank of the river Arnon, all the plain by Medeba, Heshbon and all her cities, unto Jordan and his border, the cities and the villages thereof.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

points: Gad and Reuben and the half tribe of Manasseh had already received their inheritance beyond Jordan on the east, which Moses the servant of the Lord gave them.

note.label: Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh

points: They appointed Kedesh in Galilee in mount Naphtali, Shechem in mount Ephraim, and Kirjath-arba, which is Hebron, in the mountain of Judah; and on the other side Jordan by Jericho they assigned Bezer out of the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh.

note.label: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge

points: The children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh departed from Shiloh in the land of Canaan to go into the country of Gilead, the land of their possession according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.

note.label: Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness

points: When Phinehas and the princes heard the words of the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, it pleased them. Phinehas said, This day we perceive that the LORD is among us, because ye have not committed this trespass against the Lord.

note.label: Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness

points: The thing pleased the children of Israel; they blessed God, dismantled from war, and did not go up to destroy the land where the children of Reuben and Gad dwelt.

note.label: Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness

points: The children of Reuben and Gad called the altar Ed: for it shall be a witness between us that the LORD is God.

note.label: Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness

points: The twelve sons of Israel are set down: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

points: Reuben was the firstborn of Israel, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph, and the genealogy is not reckoned after the birthright.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 5: The Tribes East of Jordan and Their Captivity

points: The sons and dwellings of Reuben are named down to Beerah, whom Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria carried away captive.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 5: The Tribes East of Jordan and Their Captivity

points: Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh had valiant men able to bear buckler and sword and skillful in war, four and forty thousand seven hundred and threescore that went to war.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 5: The Tribes East of Jordan and Their Captivity

points: God stirred up Pul, or Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, to carry away Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh. The northern kingdom was taken in waves, not all at once.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

points: Because of this the Most High stirred up the spirit of Pul, that is Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, who carried Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh into captivity unto this day.
